caption: Ngwa Nforbi v. Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. et al., San Joaquin Sup. Ct. STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094

evidence.label: General Release of All Claims, signed at delivery
evidence.quote: for sole consideration of SIXTEEN THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED FOR dollars ($0.00) or the equivalent in service/repairs to be paid to
evidence.why: Defense exhibit. Answers: Civ. Code § 1668 (no release of one's own fraud), no § 1542 waiver, contradictory consideration, no dealer signature.

evidence.label: Delivery Summary initialed 'business or agricultural'
evidence.why: Defeats consumer-arbitration protections; the cost argument rests on inability to pay instead.

evidence.label: Delivery Summary item 11
evidence.quote: I have not received any oral promises from you.
evidence.why: Aimed at the misrepresentation counts; concealment and Riverisland fraud exception answer it.

evidence.label: Buyer's order warranty disclaimer
evidence.quote: DEALER HEREBY DISCLAIMS ALL WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED
evidence.why: Hurts the contract / warranty count; fraud is not disclaimed.

evidence.label: Arbitration Agreement cost clause
evidence.quote: The costs of arbitration shall be borne equally by the Seller and Purchaser.
evidence.why: Diamond owes half of every forum cost, including the filing fee.

evidence.label: Pearson on forum cost
evidence.quote: three arbitrators would cost more than the value of the vehicle you purchased 2.5 years ago
evidence.why_reserve: Defense counsel's own cost sensitivity; for mediation.

evidence.label: Prior-owner disclosure / pre-sale repair records showing Diamond knew of the defect
evidence.why: The proof that moves the fraud claim past the as-is clause and the release.

defenses.name: General release signed at delivery (p. 23)
open_questions: What the $16,600 was supposed to be, and whether it was ever paid or performed
DocuSign Certificate of Completion: when each page was viewed and signed

defenses.name: As-is / warranty disclaimer and no-oral-promises acknowledgment
Arbitration under the Commercial Rules with costs split
Alpine formed Sept. 2, 2025, after the sale

damages.label: Documented out-of-pocket losses
damages.why_p: Documented; liability turns on proving Diamond's knowledge.

damages.label: Punitive damages (fraud)
damages.why_p: Arbitrators rarely award; needs knowledge proof.

positions.opening_basis: Aug. 31, 2026 opening to prior counsel (Evid. Code § 1152); confirm its terms before treating it as open

trigger.label: Proof that Diamond knew of the defect before the sale
trigger.note: Early band is a cost-of-defense estimate (Oct. 7 review), not a memo figure. Set the walk-away before mediation.

repricing_events.if_favorable: Diamond ordered to bear forum costs (or arbitration denied for inability to pay): defense cost rises; raise the settlement band.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: Arbitration with costs split: Plaintiff's cost exposure rises; settle value at the early band.

repricing_events.event: Prior-owner disclosure or pre-sale repair records obtained
repricing_events.if_favorable: Knowledge proven: raise oop, income, and punitive p; release and as-is defenses weaken.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: No knowledge evidence: concealment theory weakens; stay near the early band.
